title: The ScholarMaster Architecture: A Unified Reference Model for Privacy-First Intelligent Campus Systems
abstract_snippet: Current research in intelligent cyber-physical infrastructure frequently suffers from a fragmentation challenge: hardware efficiency, algorithmic accuracy, data privacy, and sociological trust are typically treated as isolated domains. paragraphs_inventory.text_snippet: The dominant architectural thesis of this paper is Constraint-First Architectural Synthesis (CFAS) . We argue that operational trust and long-term viability emerge not from post-hoc security patching or isolated subsystem tuning, but from the strict compilation of physical, legal, and operational co...

Unlike conventional software engineering paradigms that begin with feature requirements and subsequently apply security controls, CFAS initiates synthesis from the physical, thermal, and regulatory boundary limits.
The architectural invariants presented in this reference model are designed strictly to neutralize adversaries up to and including class $A_3$.

The architecture is organized into four distinct strata. While Layers 1-8 represent the data flow, the Research Series papers map to these strata to provide operational, logical, and sociological definitions.
To ensure consistency across the 19-paper research program, we formalize the ScholarMaster Invariant Namespace .
The invariant namespace defines the foundational formal contracts across the edge execution stack: a violation of any invariant results in an immediate L1 hardware exception.

Listing 1 defines the Canonical Protobuf Schema utilized to bridge the Irreversibility Boundary. By definition, the schema lacks any fields capable of holding pixel bytes or string-based personal identifiers.
